proposed_english: the able one / the sufficient one
rationale: Greek loanword ἱκανός 'sufficient, able.' Substantival use: 'the one who is able.' Lyc ⲍ-onset before ⲓ is dialectal.
Coptic ⲛⲟϥⲣⲉ 'good thing, profit, benefit.' Used here for the apostle's beneficent action toward his disciples — the 'good thing he has done for us.'
Lyc form of Sah. ⲥⲟⲡⲥⲡ̄ 'pray, request, petition.' Paired here with ⲧⲱⲃⲍ 'prayer' as the prayer-and-petition doublet.

proposed_english: a host of multitude / a great quantity
rationale: ⲧⲱⲣ may be Lyc reflex of ⲧⲱⲱⲣⲉ 'hand' used as quantifier 'handful, host,' or possibly an idiom for 'a great number.' Confidence low; flag for parallels.
Compound ϣⲁ ('until, unto') + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('outside, forth'). Idiom for 'unto-the-outside, externally, manifestly.' Used here of the outward manifestation of the indwelling single Christ in the disciples.
